subject: health
title: Mastery check: restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment
focus: restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment
essentialQuestion: What has to keep happening when no one reminds me?
privacySafeScenario: Build an independent maintenance system with a normal-week version, a hard-week fallback version, and a written restart procedure. Progress is described in terms of behaviors kept, never body measurements.
studentTask: Learner applies restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment to a new fictional scenario and records the response with the reasoning, evidence, or decision process behind it.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment, then name one check that would catch a weak claim or an unsafe step.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment without being asked for any private disclosure.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a documented process, or a cited source rather than an unsupported claim.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
adaptationChoices: The system may be written, tabled, built as a checklist, entered in a calendar, or described aloud to an adult. Any component the learner cannot perform is planned as a supported or adapted component and scored equally.
extensionChallenge: Apply restarting after a routine collapses, without self-punishment under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.

Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
